correctness.rationale: For each d>=2 count cyclotomic exponent e_d from all original 1−q^h factors. If g=gcd(d,k)>=2, first numerator progression A=floor(n/(d/g))>=2floor(n/d), and the shifted progression includes the endpoint whenever d|kn+j, so e_d>=0. If g=1, unique shifted residue r mod d gives e_d=1_{r<=n mod d}−1_{r=n mod d}, which is -1 precisely when d divides both n and j, else >=0. d=1 exponent is zero. Therefore all negative orders are exactly nontrivial divisors of u, once each, yielding [u]_q and the radical iff. Independently enumerated 968 triples with all d<=kn+j and verified complete negative spectrum; finite test does not prove universal classification.
